intent: The panel itself, portalled over the page and pinned to one edge of the viewport while its Sheet is open.
typical_uses: A form, a filter set or a record's details in a panel at the right edge
A full-width panel dropping from the top or rising from the bottom edge

dont_use_when.situation: A popup centered over the page
A floating panel anchored beside its trigger rather than to the viewport edge

invariants.text: The panel and its backdrop are in the DOM only while the sheet is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed sheet renders nothing.

Without `container`, the panel portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the panel only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.

The panel takes its accessible name from the SheetTitle inside it and its description from the SheetDescription, through `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`; without a title, pass `aria-label` on SheetContent.

Unless `initialFocus` says otherwise, opening moves focus to the first tabbable element inside the panel, which is the built-in close button when nothing before it is tabbable, or to the panel itself when it holds none or the sheet was opened by touch.

While the root's `modal` is `true` the primitive renders a transparent backdrop of its own under the panel, which blocks the page and closes the sheet on a press, so `showBackdrop={false}` alone removes the visible veil but not the blocking.

`side` pins the panel to that viewport edge and stamps it as `data-side`: `top` and `bottom` span the full width with a height sized to the content and capped at the viewport height minus 2rem; `left` and `right` span the full height at 75% of the width, capped at 24rem from a 640px viewport up. Only the edge that faces the page gets a border, and no corner is rounded.

The panel is its own vertical scroll container, a one-column grid whose column's minimum is zero, so content taller than the panel scrolls inside it and a child wider than the panel overflows inside it instead of widening it; the built-in close button scrolls with the content.

The panel has no padding of its own: every direct child other than SheetHeader, SheetFooter (which carry their own var(--space-4) padding) and the built-in close button gets a horizontal padding of var(--space-6), the first a top padding and the last one (right before the close button when it is shown) a bottom padding of var(--space-6), and direct children are spaced var(--space-6) apart. These rules carry single-class specificity, so a child's own `className` padding can override them, and then replaces the inset rather than adding to it.
The panel fades and slides 2.5rem along its own axis on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` sheet.module.css drops the slide and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Turn off `showCloseButton` without composing a SheetClose inside the panel
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep the built-in close button, or place a SheetClose in the panel, such as in the footer; a modal sheet needs a close control inside it so touch screen reader users can leave it

anti_patterns.dont: Leave out SheetTitle for a cleaner look
anti_patterns.do_instead: Render a SheetTitle and hide it visually through its `className` when the design shows no heading, so the panel keeps an accessible name

anti_patterns.dont: Set `modal={false}` on the root and keep the backdrop
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `showBackdrop={false}` here together with `modal={false}` on the root; the backdrop alone still covers the page and closes the sheet when pressed

a11y.by: the primitive's Dialog.Popup renders role dialog; sheet.test.tsx asserts getByRole('dialog') on the open panel, that the built-in close is getByRole('button', { name: 'Close' }) and takes the name from closeLabel ("renames the built-in close button via closeLabel for non-English apps"), and that Escape on the panel closes it ("closes on Escape")

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the panel portals into; an explicit null renders no panel until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

initialFocus.states: initialFocus picks the element focused on open - true for the first tabbable element (the panel itself when opened by touch), false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the opening interaction type
initialFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus picks the element focused on close - true for the trigger or the previously focused element, false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the closing interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the panel's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the panel's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, nested, nestedDialogOpen, transitionStatus). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through sheet.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside SheetContent; only its `container` is exposed, as SheetContent's own prop.
Composed inside SheetContent as the backdrop, switched by `showBackdrop` and styled by sheet.module.css.
Composed inside SheetContent as the built-in close button, switched by `showCloseButton` and named by `closeLabel`; the exported SheetClose is the same primitive for a consumer-composed close action.

good.title: A left-edge panel with a scrolling body between header and footer
A panel portalled into a themed subtree, with a localized close label

bad.title: A made-up prop for the panel's edge
bad.why: SheetContent has no `position` prop; the edge is `side`, so this panel still opens at the right edge.

capabilities.name: close_button
capabilities.description: Default true: the panel renders a close (X) button after its children, a ghost kit Button placed var(--space-4) from the top and right edges, whose accessible name is `closeLabel`; it is the panel's only built-in close control, and pressing it closes the sheet.

capabilities.name: backdrop
capabilities.description: Default true: a fixed layer behind the panel covers the page with a light var(--overlay-panel) tint and, where the browser supports it, a blur of what is behind, and a press on it closes the sheet.
